_note: Task-level evals for an OUTWARD-FACING, side-effecting skill. Running these for real creates a GitHub repository, runs git/gh, and writes files to disk. DO NOT auto-run them through the skill-creator harness against a live account. To execute: use a throwaway GitHub namespace and a temp directory, or stub the gh/git steps. The expectations describe the scaffold a correct run must produce.

evals.prompt: Start a brand-new Python project called widget-parser using our standard tooling. It's a small CLI library.
evals.expected_output: The skill scaffolds a new project directory using the copier-astral template with uv, ruff, and pytest, sets up a private GitHub repo with branch protection and a feature-branch workflow, adds a project CLAUDE.md, and uses Google-style docstrings.
expectations: A new project directory named 'widget-parser' is created from the copier-astral template (not hand-rolled)
Dependency and environment management uses uv
Tests use pytest (pure pytest, no unittest)
A private GitHub repository is created with branch protection enabled
A feature-branch workflow is established (no direct commits to the default branch)

evals.prompt: I'm in an existing repo and want to add a caching layer. Set me up.
evals.expected_output: The skill does NOT trigger / declines, because this is work inside an existing project, not bootstrapping a new one. (Negative behavioral check: new-python-project is bootstrap-only.)
expectations: The skill recognizes this is not a new-project bootstrap and does not scaffold a fresh project
No copier template is run and no new GitHub repository is created for this request
